title: Mocha Ice Cream Pie
changes_from_base: A baked chocolate crumb crust brushed with chocolate sauce, filled with a home-churned no-cook mocha ice cream and topped with whipped cream, instead of sponge layers.
summary: A coffee-and-cocoa ice cream pie in a chocolate biscuit crust, piled with cream and finished with a drizzle of chocolate sauce.
equipment: ice-cream maker (bowl frozen at least 24 h)
stand mixer or hand mixer with whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
chocolate sandwich biscuits, broken into small pieces (optional)

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Press a mix of 206 g chocolate biscuit crumbs, 28 g icing sugar, ¼ tsp salt and 57 g melted butter over the base and sides of the pie tin, line with foil and baking beans and bake at 190 °C for 12 min, then remove the foil and beans and bake for 4-6 min more until shiny; cool completely.

steps.title: Brush
steps.text: Warm 99 g chocolate sauce until pourable and brush it all over the inside of the crust, then freeze while you make the ice cream.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Whisk 227 g cold milk with 149 g sugar, 11 g espresso powder and 11 g cocoa until the sugar dissolves, stir in 454 g cold double cream and vanilla, then churn in the ice-cream maker, folding in the broken chocolate sandwich biscuits at the end.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip the topping double cream with icing sugar to firm peaks.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Spoon the mocha ice cream into the crust and spread or pipe the whipped cream on top.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for about 2 h until firm, thawing for 15-20 min if it has been frozen for longer.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drizzle with extra chocolate sauce, scatter over extra broken biscuits if using, and serve.

tips: Warm the chocolate sauce until pourable, brush it all over the inside of the cooled crust and freeze while you make the ice cream, so it sets into a firm layer under the filling.
Make sure the ice-cream maker bowl has been in the freezer for at least 24 h before churning.
Thaw the pie for 15-20 min if it has been in the freezer longer than 2 h, so it is easier to slice.
safety: The ice cream contains espresso powder, so bear its caffeine content in mind if serving children or anyone avoiding caffeine.
storage: Wrapped well, the pie keeps in the freezer for up to 2 weeks.
